description: Differentiation, limits, integration, complex numbers, series, Taylor approximation, matrices, linear systems, and eigenvalue methods for Level 1 Math I.
instructions: All main questions carry the same number of marks.
Show sufficient working to justify each answer.
Begin each main question on a new page.
label: Paper 1

questions.stem: This question concerns inverse trigonometric differentiation, a limit that may be evaluated using L'Hopital's rule, and a first-principles derivative.
questions.title: Inverse functions, limits, and first principles

parts.answer:
Use the chain rule with \(u=2x\). Since
\[
\frac{d}{du}\sin^{-1}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^2}},
\]
we get
\[
f'(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-(2x)^2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}.
\]
At \(x=\frac{1}{4}\),
\[
f'\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}}}.
\]
Thus
\[
f'\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3/4}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Differentiate \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}(2x)\), where \(|x|<\frac{1}{2}\), and evaluate \(f'\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)\).

parts.answer:
As \(x\to0\), the numerator and denominator both tend to \(0\). Applying L'Hopital's rule once gives
\[
\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{3x}-1-3x}{x^2}=\lim_{x\to0}\frac{3e^{3x}-3}{2x}.
\]
This is still a \(0/0\) form, so apply L'Hopital's rule again:
\[
\lim_{x\to0}\frac{3e^{3x}-3}{2x}=\lim_{x\to0}\frac{9e^{3x}}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{3x}-1-3x}{x^2}=\frac{9}{2}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \lim_{x\to0}\frac{e^{3x}-1-3x}{x^2}\).

parts.answer:
First find \(f'(x)\) using the chain rule. Since
\[
f(x)=\sin^{-1}(2x),
\]
let \(u=2x\), so \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}u\) and \(du/dx=2\). Then
\[
f'(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}\cdot\frac{du}{dx}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}.
\]
At \(x=\frac{1}{4}\),
\[
f'\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}.
\]
The point on the curve is
\[
\left(\frac{1}{4},\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)=\left(\frac{1}{4},\frac{\pi}{6}\right).
\]
Using the point-slope form, the tangent line is
\[
y-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}\left(x-\frac{1}{4}\right).
\]
In standard form, this is
\[
4\sqrt3\,x-12\,y+\pi-\sqrt3=0.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent line to \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}(2x)\) at \(x=\frac{1}{4}\), giving your answer in the form \(y=mx+c\).

questions.stem: This question uses trigonometric powers, a reduction formula, and partial fractions.
questions.title: Integration techniques

parts.answer:
Use
\[
\sin^2x=\frac{1-\cos2x}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
\sin^4x=\left(\frac{1-\cos2x}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1-2\cos2x+\cos^22x}{4}.
\]
Also
\[
\cos^22x=\frac{1+\cos4x}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\sin^4x=\frac{3}{8}-\frac{1}{2}\cos2x+\frac{1}{8}\cos4x.
\]
Therefore
\[
\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^4x\,dx=\left[\frac{3x}{8}-\frac{1}{4}\sin2x+\frac{1}{32}\sin4x\right]_0^{\pi/2}.
\]
The sine terms vanish at both endpoints, so
\[
\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^4x\,dx=\frac{3\pi}{16}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^4x\,dx\).

parts.answer:
Let
\[
J_n=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^n x\,dx.
\]
For \(n>1\), use \(\tan^2x=\sec^2x-1\):
\[
J_n=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x(\sec^2x-1)\,dx.
\]
Therefore
\[
J_n=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x\sec^2x\,dx-\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x\,dx.
\]
For the first integral, let \(u=\tan x\), so \(du=\sec^2x\,dx\). The limits are \(u=0\) when \(x=0\), and \(u=1\) when \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\). Hence
\[
\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^{n-2}x\sec^2x\,dx=\int_0^1u^{n-2}\,du=\frac{1}{n-1}.
\]
Thus
\[
J_n=\frac{1}{n-1}-J_{n-2}.
\]
For \(J_4\),
\[
J_4=\frac{1}{3}-J_2.
\]
Also
\[
J_2=\int_0^{\pi/4}(\sec^2x-1)\,dx=\left[\tan x-x\right]_0^{\pi/4}=1-\frac{\pi}{4}.
\]
Therefore
\[
J_4=\frac{1}{3}-\left(1-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{2}{3}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Let \(J_n=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan^n x\,dx\). Show that \(J_n=\frac{1}{n-1}-J_{n-2}\) for \(n>1\), and hence find \(J_4\).

parts.answer:
Factor the denominator:
\[
x^2+x-6=(x+3)(x-2).
\]
Write
\[
\frac{5x+1}{x^2+x-6}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B}{x+3}.
\]
Multiplying through gives
\[
5x+1=A(x+3)+B(x-2).
\]
Equating coefficients,
\[
A+B=5,\qquad 3A-2B=1.
\]
From \(B=5-A\),
\[
3A-2(5-A)=1,\qquad 5A=11.
\]
Thus \(A=\frac{11}{5}\) and \(B=\frac{14}{5}\). Hence
\[
\int\frac{5x+1}{x^2+x-6}\,dx=\frac{11}{5}\ln|x-2|+\frac{14}{5}\ln|x+3|+C.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int\frac{5x+1}{x^2+x-6}\,dx\).

questions.stem: This question uses De Moivre's theorem, roots of a complex polynomial, and exponential form.
questions.title: Complex powers and roots

parts.answer:
By De Moivre's theorem,
\[
(\cos	heta+i\sin	heta)^4=\cos4	heta+i\sin4	heta.
\]
Expanding the left-hand side, the imaginary part is
\[
4\cos^3	heta\sin	heta-4\cos	heta\sin^3	heta.
\]
Equating imaginary parts gives
\[
\sin4	heta=4\cos^3	heta\sin	heta-4\cos	heta\sin^3	heta.
\]
Factor the right-hand side:
\[
\sin4	heta=4\sin	heta\cos	heta(\cos^2	heta-\sin^2	heta).
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use De Moivre's theorem to show that \(\sin4	heta=4\sin	heta\cos	heta(\cos^2	heta-\sin^2	heta)\).

parts.answer:
Write
\[
8i=8e^{i(\pi/2+2m\pi)},\qquad m\in\mathbb Z.
\]
The cube roots have modulus
\[
8^{1/3}=2.
\]
Their arguments are
\[
\frac{\pi/2+2m\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{2m\pi}{3}.
\]
Taking \(m=0,1,2\), the roots are
\[
z=2e^{i(\pi/6+2k\pi/3)},\qquad k=0,1,2.
\]
In rectangular form these are
\[
\sqrt3+i,\quad -\sqrt3+i,\quad -2i.
\]
So
\[
z^3-8i=0
\]
has those three roots.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve \(z^3-8i=0\), giving all roots in exponential form and rectangular form.

parts.answer:
Rewrite the number as
\[
w=e^{2-i\pi/6}=e^2e^{-i\pi/6}.
\]
The modulus is the positive scale factor
\[
|w|=e^2.
\]
The argument is
\[
\arg w=-\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]
In rectangular form,
\[
w=e^2\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right).
\]
Thus
\[
w=e^2\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{i}{2}\right)=\frac{e^2\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{e^2}{2}i.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Interpret \(w=e^{2-i\pi/6}\) in exponential form by stating its modulus and argument, then write it in rectangular form.

questions.stem: This question uses comparison, ratio tests, and endpoint checks for a power series.
questions.title: Convergence tests and endpoints

parts.answer:
Let
\[
a_n=\frac{n^2+1}{3n^3+1}.
\]
Compare with the harmonic series term \(b_n=\frac{1}{n}\). Compute the limit comparison:
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{b_n}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{n(n^2+1)}{3n^3+1}.
\]
Divide numerator and denominator by \(n^3\):
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1+\frac{1}{n^2}}{3+\frac{1}{n^3}}=\frac{1}{3}.
\]
This limit is positive and finite. Since
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n}
\]
diverges, the limit comparison test shows that
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2+1}{3n^3+1}
\]
diverges.
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use limit comparison to determine whether \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2+1}{3n^3+1}\) converges.

parts.answer:
Let
\[
a_n=\left(\frac{2n+1}{5n+3}\right)^n.
\]
Use the root test:
\[
\sqrt[n]{|a_n|}=\frac{2n+1}{5n+3}.
\]
Taking the limit gives
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n|}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{2n+1}{5n+3}=\frac{2}{5}.
\]
Since \(\frac{2}{5}<1\), the root test shows that
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{2n+1}{5n+3}\right)^n
\]
converges absolutely.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the root test to determine whether \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{2n+1}{5n+3}\right)^n\) converges.

parts.answer:
Let
\[
a_n(x)=\frac{(x-3)^n}{n^2 5^n}.
\]
Use the ratio test on absolute values:
\[
\left|\frac{a_{n+1}(x)}{a_n(x)}\right|=\left|\frac{(x-3)^{n+1}}{(n+1)^2 5^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{n^2 5^n}{(x-3)^n}\right|.
\]
So
\[
\left|\frac{a_{n+1}(x)}{a_n(x)}\right|=\frac{n^2}{(n+1)^2}\cdot\frac{|x-3|}{5}.
\]
Taking the limit gives
\[
L=\frac{|x-3|}{5}.
\]
The series converges absolutely when \(L<1\), so
\[
|x-3|<5,\qquad -2<x<8.
\]
At \(x=8\), the series is
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2},
\]
which converges. At \(x=-2\), the series is
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n^2},
\]
which converges absolutely because \(\sum 1/n^2\) converges. Therefore the interval of convergence is
\[
[-2,8].
\]
The radius of convergence is \(5\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the radius and interval of convergence of \(\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(x-3)^n}{n^2 5^n}\), including endpoint tests.

questions.section: Section E: Taylor Series and Matrices
questions.stem: This question combines Taylor approximation with Lagrange remainders and matrix linear dependence.
questions.title: Approximation and dependence

parts.answer:
For \(f(x)=\cos x\),
\[
f'(x)=-\sin x,\quad f''(x)=-\cos x,\quad f'''(x)=\sin x.
\]
At \(x=0\),
\[
f(0)=1,\quad f'(0)=0,\quad f''(0)=-1,\quad f'''(0)=0.
\]
Thus the cubic Taylor polynomial about \(0\) is
\[
P_3(x)=1-\frac{x^2}{2}.
\]
At \(x=0.2\),
\[
P_3(0.2)=1-\frac{0.2^2}{2}=1-0.02=0.98.
\]
So \(\cos(0.2)\approx0.98\).
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the cubic Taylor polynomial for \(\cos x\) about \(0\), and use it to approximate \(\cos(0.2)\).

parts.answer:
The Lagrange remainder after degree \(3\) is
\[
R_3(x)=\frac{f^{(4)}(\xi)}{4!}x^4
\]
for some \(\xi\) between \(0\) and \(x\). Since
\[
f^{(4)}(x)=\cos x,
\]
we have
\[
|f^{(4)}(x)|\le1.
\]
Therefore, for \(x=0.2\),
\[
|R_3(0.2)|\le\frac{1}{4!}(0.2)^4=\frac{0.0016}{24}.
\]
Hence
\[
|R_3(0.2)|\le 0.0000667\quad\text{approximately}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the Lagrange remainder to bound the error in the approximation from part (a).

parts.answer:
Put the three vectors as columns of a matrix. They are linearly dependent exactly when the determinant is zero:
\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&1\\0&1&k\\2&1&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Compute
\[
\det M=1\det\begin{pmatrix}1&k\\1&3\end{pmatrix}-2\det\begin{pmatrix}0&k\\2&3\end{pmatrix}+1\det\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The minors are
\[
3-k,\qquad -2k,\qquad -2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\det M=(3-k)-2(-2k)-2=1+3k.
\]
Set this equal to zero:
\[
1+3k=0.
\]
Thus the vectors are linearly dependent when
\[
k=-\frac{1}{3}.
\]
They are linearly independent for every other real value of \(k\).
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the value of \(k\) for which the vectors \((1,0,2)\), \((2,1,1)\), and \((1,k,3)\) are linearly dependent.

questions.stem:
Consider the parameter-dependent system
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+y+z&=2,\\
x+2y+3z&=5,\\
2x+3y+az&=b.
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.title: Parameters and solution geometry

parts.answer:
The coefficient matrix is
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\2&3&a\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Compute its determinant:
\[
\det A=1\det\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\3&a\end{pmatrix}-1\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\2&a\end{pmatrix}+1\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The minors are
\[
2a-9,\qquad a-6,\qquad -1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\det A=(2a-9)-(a-6)-1=a-4.
\]
The system has a unique solution exactly when
\[
a\ne4.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the values of \(a\) for which the system has a unique solution.

parts.answer:
Use the augmented matrix
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&1&1&2\\1&2&3&5\\2&3&a&b\end{array}\right).
\]
Apply \(R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1\) and \(R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1\):
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&1&1&2\\0&1&2&3\\0&1&a-2&b-4\end{array}\right).
\]
Then apply \(R_3\leftarrow R_3-R_2\):
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}1&1&1&2\\0&1&2&3\\0&0&a-4&b-7\end{array}\right).
\]
When \(a=4\), the last row becomes
\[
\left(\begin{array}{ccc|c}0&0&0&b-7\end{array}\right).
\]
Thus if \(b\ne7\), the system is inconsistent and has no solution. If \(b=7\), the last row is \(0=0\), leaving one free variable and infinitely many solutions.
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Classify the non-unique cases using row reduction.

parts.answer:
The three equations represent three planes in \(\mathbb R^3\). If \(a\ne4\), the coefficient matrix is invertible, so the planes meet in exactly one point. If \(a=4\) and \(b\ne7\), row reduction gives a contradiction, so the planes have no common point. If \(a=4\) and \(b=7\), one variable is free, so the common solution set is a line.

For the homogeneous system in the singular case \(a=4\), solve
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+y+z&=0,\\
y+2z&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(z=t\). Then \(y=-2t\), and
\[
x-2t+t=0,\qquad x=t.
\]
Therefore the homogeneous solution set is
\[
(x,y,z)=t(1,-2,1),\qquad t\in\mathbb R.
\]
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe the solution geometry in each case, and find the homogeneous solution set when \(a=4\).

questions.section: Section G: Eigenvalues and Matrix Structure
questions.title: Diagonalisation and matrix structure

parts.answer:
Compute
\[
A\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\3\end{pmatrix}=3\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \((1,1)^T\) has eigenvalue \(3\). Also
\[
A\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}=1\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
so \((1,-1)^T\) has eigenvalue \(1\). Therefore
\[
P=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad D=\begin{pmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since \(\det P=-2\ne0\), \(P\) is invertible and
\[
A=PDP^{-1}.
\]
parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Diagonalise \(A\) by constructing suitable matrices \(P\) and \(D\).

parts.answer:
From \(A=PDP^{-1}\), powers satisfy
\[
A^n=PD^nP^{-1}.
\]
Here
\[
D^n=\begin{pmatrix}3^n&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since
\[
P^{-1}=\frac{1}{-2}\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
we get
\[
A^n=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}3^n&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Multiplying gives
\[
A^n=\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}3^n+1&3^n-1\\3^n-1&3^n+1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the diagonalisation to find a formula for \(A^n\), where \(n\) is a positive integer.

parts.answer:
Statement (i) is true. If \(Q\) is orthogonal, then \(Q^TQ=I\). For any vector \(\mathbf x\),
\[
\|Q\mathbf x\|^2=(Q\mathbf x)^T(Q\mathbf x)=\mathbf x^TQ^TQ\mathbf x=\mathbf x^T\mathbf x=\|\mathbf x\|^2.
\]
Therefore orthogonal matrices preserve lengths.

Statement (ii) is false. A real matrix can be both symmetric and skew-symmetric only if it is the zero matrix. If \(M^T=M\) and \(M^T=-M\), then
\[
M=-M.
\]
Hence
\[
2M=0,\qquad M=0.
\]
So a nonzero real matrix cannot be both symmetric and skew-symmetric.
parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Decide whether each statement is true or false, giving a proof or counterexample. (i) Orthogonal matrices preserve vector lengths. (ii) A nonzero real matrix can be both symmetric and skew-symmetric.
